33 Four point charges, each of charge Q, are placed on the edge of an insulating disc of radius r.
The disc rotates at a rate of n revolutions per unit time.

hints: Notice the disc carries four separate charges each of charge $Q$ on its edge, so find the total charge that goes round together.
Recall current is rate of flow of charge, $I = \Delta Q / \Delta t$, where $\Delta Q$ is the charge passing a fixed point in time $\Delta t$.
Use the wording $n$ revolutions per unit time to find how much charge passes a fixed point in unit time, and check why radius $r$ is not needed.
walkthrough: Identify the moving charge from the diagram: four point charges each $Q$ fixed to the edge, so total circulating charge is $Q_{total} = 4Q$.
State the governing rule for equivalent current: $I = \Delta Q / \Delta t$, the charge passing a fixed point at the edge per unit time.
Find the time for one revolution: $n$ revolutions occur per unit time, so one revolution takes $T = 1/n$.
Calculate the charge passing per unit time: in one period $T$ the charge $4Q$ passes, so $I = 4Q / T = 4Q / (1/n) = 4Qn$.
Check units: $[Q]$ is coulomb and $[n]$ is $\text{s}^{-1}$, so $[4Qn]$ is $\text{C s}^{-1} = \text{A}$, while radius $r$ cancels out of the rate argument. This is option A.

A.explanation: Total charge $4Q$ passes a fixed point $n$ times per unit time, so $I = 4Qn$.

B.explanation: Dividing by $n$ is wrong because $n$ is revolutions per unit time, so charge per unit time is multiplied by $n$.

C.explanation: The circumference $2\pi r$ is not needed because current is charge per unit time, not charge per unit length.

D.explanation: Radius $r$ does not affect the rate of charge flow past a point, so any expression containing $r$ is incorrect.
